classification.difficultyReason: Parts a to d are signposted routine procedures: gradient, inclination angle, point-gradient equation, midpoint, and a product-of-gradients perpendicularity check. Part e needs interpretation, since BD is the perpendicular bisector of AC and so BA = BC. Part f needs the student to see that BD is the height, which is a small reframing. Part g is the hardest essential demand and is unsignposted. The student must reframe the rhombus as ABCE with diagonals AC and BE bisecting each other at D, then reflect B through D to get E. This links several earlier results, so it is a bit harder than p67-q9, which has similar linked gradient and isosceles ideas. It is still easier than A5, because the reframing is guided by the earlier parts and the diagram and involves no open-ended search.
